# Judith Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_012_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And he commanded them to bring her in where his silver vessels were set out, and he ordered that she be served from his own food and his own wine.

**2** But Judith said, "I cannot eat from these things, lest there be an offense; but provision will be made for me from what I have brought."

**3** And Holofernes said to her, "But if the things you brought with you run out, where will we get more to give you the same? For there is no one of your people with us."

**4** And Judith said to him, "As your soul lives, my lord, your servant will not use up the things she has with her before the LORD accomplishes by my hand what he has purposed."

**5** And the servants of Holofernes brought her into the tent, and she slept until the middle of the night. And she rose before the morning watch and sent a message to Holofernes, saying,

**6** "Let my lord now command that your servant be permitted to go out to prayer."

**7** And Holofernes commanded his bodyguards not to hinder her. And she stayed in the camp three days, and she went out each night into the valley of Bethulia and bathed herself in the camp at the spring of water.

**8** And when she came up from the water, she entreated the LORD God of Israel to direct her way for the uplifting of the sons of his people.

**9** And she came in clean and remained in the tent until she took her food toward evening.

**10** And on the fourth day Holofernes made a banquet for his servants alone, and he did not invite any of his officers.

**11** And he said to Bagoas, the eunuch who had charge of all his affairs, "Go now and persuade this Hebrew woman who is with you to come to us and eat and drink with us.

**12** For behold, it is a disgrace for our side if we let such a woman go without having intercourse with her; for if we do not seduce her, she will laugh at us."

**13** And Bagoas went from the presence of Holofernes and came in to her and said, "Let the fair young woman not be reluctant to come to my lord and to be honored in his presence, and to drink wine with us in gladness, and to become this day like one of the daughters of the Assyrians who serve in the house of Nebuchadnezzar."

**14** And Judith said to him, "Who am I to refuse my lord? Whatever is pleasing in his eyes I will do with haste; and this will be my joy until the day of my death."

**15** And she rose and adorned herself with her clothing and all her feminine adornment. And her servant went ahead and spread on the ground for her before Holofernes the fleeces which she had received from Bagoas for her daily use, to recline upon while eating.

**16** And Judith came in and reclined, and the heart of Holofernes was ravished by her, and his soul was stirred, and he greatly desired to have intercourse with her; for he had been watching for an opportunity to seduce her from the day he first saw her.

**17** And Holofernes said to her, "Drink now and be glad with us."

**18** And Judith said, "I will drink now, my lord, for my life is magnified this day above all my days since I was born."

**19** And she took what her servant had prepared and ate and drank before him.

**20** And Holofernes was delighted by her and drank very much wine — more than he had ever drunk in one single day since he was born.

---
*EMET notes: v. 7 — "spring of water" (pege tou hydatos) is the specific water source at Bethulia mentioned in earlier chapters. v. 12 — the Greek is explicit about Holofernes' intentions; "have intercourse" renders the euphemistic syngenesthai (lit. "be together with"). v. 16 — "soul was stirred" renders psychē autou etarachthē; "ravished" renders the heart metaphor literally. v. 18 — Judith's toast is deeply ironic: her life is indeed magnified this day.*
